# RedwoodSDK: Type-Safe Navigation with linkFor

## Background
A RedwoodSDK project is pre-installed at `/home/user/myapp`. Use `linkFor` from `rwsdk/router` to build a typed `link` helper, and use it inside server components so that every link in your HTML output is generated from the typed helper (no hard-coded path strings on the page).

## Requirements
Extend `src/worker.tsx` with the routes below (all under the existing `render(Document, ...)` block) and create a `src/app/shared/links.ts` file that exports a typed `link` constant created from `linkFor<App>()` (where `App` is the type of the default export from `src/worker.tsx`). Use that `link` helper inside the page components.

- `GET /home`: server component HTML must contain an `<a>` element whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/about")` and whose visible text is `About`. It must also contain an `<a>` whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/users/:id", { id: "42" })` and whose visible text is `Show user 42`.
- `GET /about`: HTML must contain an `<a>` whose `href` is generated by calling `link("/home")` and whose visible text is `Back to home`.
- `GET /users/:id`: HTML must contain the text `User profile: <id>` (with the URL param substituted).

I have successfully extended the RedwoodSDK project with type-safe navigation using `linkFor`.

Here is a summary of the implementation details:

1. **Created/Updated `src/app/shared/links.ts`**:
   - Resolved the circular dependency issue in TypeScript by importing the type of the default export of `src/worker.tsx` as `App` and passing it to `linkFor<App>()`.

2. **Created New Page Components**:
   - `src/app/pages/home-page.tsx`: Renders the `/home` page. It generates links to `/about` and `/users/:id` (with `id: "42"`) using the typed `link` helper.
   - `src/app/pages/about-page.tsx`: Renders the `/about` page. It generates a link back to `/home` using the typed `link` helper.
   - `src/app/pages/user-page.tsx`: Renders the `/users/:id` page. It dynamically accesses and displays the route param (`User profile: <id>`).

3. **Extended `src/worker.tsx`**:
   - Imported the new page components (`HomePage`, `AboutPage`, `UserPage`).
   - Registered the routes (`/home`, `/about`, and `/users/:id`) under the existing `render(Document, ...)` block.
   - Exported the `App` type representing the default application definition to allow `links.ts` to perform type-safe routing.

4. **Verification**:
   - Ran `npm run check` and verified that the TypeScript compiler successfully type-checks all routes and parameters with zero errors.
   - Verified that using any invalid route string or parameter types inside `link()` correctly triggers a compile-time error.
